blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how economists make sense of complex data? They use tools like tables, charts, and graphs to simplify and present information clearly.

blocks.markdown: In economics, data is often presented in various forms to make it easier to understand and analyze. The most common tools used are tables, charts, and graphs. These tools help economists to visualize data, identify trends, and make informed decisions.

blocks.title: Definition: Tools of Economic Analysis
blocks.text: Tools of economic analysis include tables, charts, graphs, and measures of central tendency like mean, median, and mode.

blocks.markdown:
### Tables
Tables organize data into rows and columns, making it easy to compare different sets of data. For example, a table can show the monthly sales figures of a market.

### Charts and Graphs
Charts and graphs, such as bar charts and line graphs, visually represent data, allowing for quick interpretation of trends and patterns.

blocks.title: Calculating the Mean
blocks.prompt: Calculate the mean of the following data set: 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.

steps.text: Divide the sum by the number of data points: $\frac{100}{5} = 20$.

blocks.answer: The mean of the data set is 20.

blocks.markdown: Graphs are particularly useful because they provide a visual representation of data, making it easier to identify trends and patterns over time.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When interpreting graphs, pay attention to the axes labels and the scale used. This will help you understand the data being presented accurately.

points: Tables, charts, and graphs are essential tools in economic analysis.
The mean, median, and mode are measures of central tendency used to summarize data.
